points.description: States that the learning rate controls the speed/rate of convergence (e.g. a low learning rate gives slow, overdamped convergence). Equivalent wording is acceptable.

States a danger of a high learning rate: convergence becomes underdamped/zigzagging/oscillatory, and/or if the learning rate exceeds a critical value learning becomes unstable/diverges. Equivalent wording is acceptable.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the role of the learning rate (it controls convergence speed) and a danger of too high a learning rate (zigzagging/oscillation or instability/divergence). A low-rate slow-convergence detail may support P1 but is not required. No marks are given for merely defining learning rate without linking it to convergence speed or to a danger.
